extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and instrument-makers (readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and reporting experimental/observational natural-philosophy results and mathematical/theoretical solutions (late-17th-century style): detailed apparatus description, measurements, microscopy, botanical/geological description, and algebraic derivations in dioptrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus integrity and repeatable trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe apparatus and repeated trials; note failures and causes (e.g., cork 'not sound' allowing sea-water to soak through).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give full details of how instruments or containers were prepared and attached (stopping and tying the bottle, fastening to plumbing-rope, use of a lead weight). Report repeated experiments, the exact differences in setup (different corks, sizes), and how those differences affected outcomes (full bottle vs half full; cork pressed into neck vs not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify observations (distance, time, frequency, regularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report numerical values for phenomena (e.g., well ebb/flow amplitude, timing, frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report measured distances (e.g., 'from high water to low water-mark ... somewhat more than 5 inches'), timing with a watch (e.g., 'the flux and reflux ... was performed in about two minutes'; 'about 16 times in an hour'), and note regularity or variability (when it sometimes stood lowest for 2–3 minutes; sometimes 20 times an hour). Include sensory observations (bubbles seen when rising) linked to the measured phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide site/context description and local relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Give precise contextual information about the observation site (relative elevation, distance from landmarks, surrounding topography and geology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State position relative to sea level and towns (e.g., 'halfway up the hill', 'about a mile and a half from Brixam to top of the hill'). Describe nearby country, soil composition, mineral impregnation (taste of water, not brackish, no mineral impregnation), and any local uses (country people use the water in fevers). Such context informs interpretation of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphological and comparative botanical description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plant parts in detail (leaf size/shape, flowers, fruit, seeds) and compare to known taxa for identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurements and qualitative descriptors (e.g., 'leaves ... an inch and half long, and an inch broad', 'flowers milk-white, pentapetalous, smell like jasmine', 'oval berry ... black aromatic seeds'). Compare the specimen to familiar genera ('I cannot reduce it to any of our kind of plants, so well as to the periclymenum') and record uses and preparations (boiling bark with carminative seeds, dosing, observed therapeutic effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical organization of materia medica
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange materia medica succinctly and naturally, providing genera, specific synonyms/differences and uses, but avoid uncritical praise of inert or incongruous drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compendium should be better arranged than predecessors and give succinct, accurate descriptions with characters and synonyms. Yet be cautious and critical of endorsements of inert or inappropriate remedies ('lavish in the praises of inert or incongruous drugs').

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural recommendation must consider local suitability and comparative yields
rubrics_metrics.description: When recommending a crop or improvement (e.g., maize), compare expected produce and effects on land with existing crops and consider local conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume success in a new region; compare yield per acre, nutritional equivalence (goodness equal to peas), and potential land impoverishment. Note multiple species/varieties (e.g., 'two really distinct species of maize') and report observed differences in stature and seed ripening across locales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological and palaeontological field reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report occurrences of fossilized shells, petrified teeth, bones, and rock composition with measurements and inferred extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe thickness and distribution of shell deposits (e.g., 'veins of these rocky shells 3 or 4 yards thick'), find locations (foot of a hill, several yards deep), sizes of blocks and inferred composition (burning for lime), and curiosities (petrified teeth, whale backbone). Use such facts to infer past environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopy and seed/embryo anatomy methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dissection and microscope to reveal seed structure: embryo, enclosing leaves/films, nutritive tissues, ligaments; document proportions and germination behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open seeds carefully, describe each layer encountered (hard shell, whitish coat, leaves wrapping the embryo), count and measure components (e.g., 'four small leaves', 'seed 7 times longer... embryo 300 times smaller'), test germination conditions (hot moist sand, wet sand) and report growth (shooting of root, appearance of leaves). Compare across many species and conclude generalities (e.g., 'there is no seed but what has its embryo plant').

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic description of animal tissues and cautious inference of function
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe microstructure (fibres, globules, capillary vessels) and propose mechanisms grounded in observation, while acknowledging limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sizes and arrangements (optic nerve made of many fibres filled with globules; crystalline humour axes), note differences among species, and infer possible physiological roles (movement of globules effecting sight). Explicitly state when a proposed mechanism is speculative ('if it be not allowed ... yet it must be granted...'), and emphasize continual generation/nourishment where observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record experimental conditions for crystallization and dynamic observations
rubrics_metrics.description: When observing salt or particle formation (in vinegars, juices, spirits), record the preparation, duration, temperature treatments, and interactions with added materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note timescales ('after 8 or 10 days'), manipulations (freezing, settling, adding crabs'-eyes), and transient phenomena (particles forming 'in an instant, like lightning'). Describe particle shapes and stages (cavities, imperfect forms, joined particles) and any interactions with biological fluids (spirit of sal ammoniac dissolving blood-globules over time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for algebraic/theoretical solutions: generality and reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 'full and adequate solutions' that represent all possible cases in one general theorem and permit reduction to subordinate/special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer general theorems that 'represent all the possible cases at one view' and can be reduced to propositions and demonstrated; use such general results to derive theorems for all lens types by changing signs or parameters. Show how a single solution covers double-convex, double-concave, plano-convex, meniscus, converging/diverging rays, and limiting cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dioptrics modeling conventions and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: In lens-focus problems include lens thickness and refractive-index ratios in a universal equation, adopt clear sign conventions for concave/convex surfaces and object distances, and present simplifications for limiting cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define variables (radii r and p, thickness t, object distance d, refractive ratio m:n), explain sign conventions (concave radii or distances taken negative), include the thickness in the general equation for perfection though it may often be negligible, and show the simplifications (thin-lens, d infinite) and numeric examples for typical refractive indices (glass 3:2, water, diamond). Make explicit how to substitute to obtain rules for each particular lens-case and show how to derive focus, or invert to find object distance or refractive ratio when other data are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reader prerequisites and balance completeness with accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate assumed prior knowledge (analytical multiplication/division rules) and be mindful of the trade-off between completeness for experts and clarity for less skilled readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state prerequisites ('I here suppose my reader acquainted with the rules of analytical multiplication and division') and note the difficulty in pleasing both expert analysts and less skilful readers; aim to present sufficient reductions and examples to make general theorems usable by both audiences.
